solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Just being next to fiendish leader is hideous

indicators.note: being next to says the two pieces sit side by side
the leader of the word fiendish is its opening letter

parts.note: just, as in fair and lawful, means rightful

explanation.surface: A moral complaint: merely standing beside a wicked ringleader is an ugly thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like 'merely' but means fair, lawful.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal intensifiers for something dreadful or very ugly; synonyms.

clue.text: Second half's disastrous

indicators.note: a disastrous arrangement is a wrecked one, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sports commentator laments that the second half went badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like an adjective for 'half' but is the noun for a moment; the letters of HALFS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: In a flash means in an instant, so the noun is a very brief moment, a synonym for a second.

clue.text: I recite principal pieces from Threepenny Opera in private

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: private, as in inner thoughts, means inner

indicators.note: the principal piece of each word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A performer confides they recite parts of Brecht and Weill's Threepenny Opera alone.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the voice of the answer itself: someone who chants or recites might say 'I recite'.
explanation.definitionFit: One who intones chants or recites in a monotone, so the word describes the speaker of the phrase.

clue.text: Fellow outlaw accepting lift from Scottish location

parts.note: a fellow is a male, he

indicators.note: accepting means taking the other piece inside

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it
a lift in a car is a ride

explanation.surface: A man and a bandit hitch a ride away from somewhere in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hebrides are island groups off Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to or coming from the Hebrides, islands of Scotland.

clue.text: Part of breakfast perhaps spilt on chef's tart

indicators.note: spilt things are scattered and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some breakfast item has been slopped over a cook's pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the answer as one example of a breakfast dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread dipped in egg and fried is an example of a morning dish.

clue.text: Drag bird up out of a lake

indicators.note: out of says the lake abbreviation is removed
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a gull is a seabird
L is the standard abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone hauls a bird out of a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GULL into LLUG; 'out of' takes away one L.
explanation.definitionFit: To drag something heavy is to haul or carry it laboriously; synonyms.

clue.text: Round edge of rock, swimmer sunbathes

indicators.note: round says the fish goes around the other letter

parts.note: a swimmer can be a fish such as a bass

indicators.note: the edge of rock here is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone swims round the edge of a rock, then sunbathes on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmer' wants to be a person but is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie in warm sunlight is to sunbathe; synonyms.

clue.text: Great British PM in Australia promoting queen

indicators.note: promoting means moving the queen letter further up the word

parts.note: Australians call the afternoon arvo
R, for regina, is the queen

explanation.surface: A British Prime Minister, down under, promotes the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM' looks like a Prime Minister but means afternoon; Australian slang ARVO becomes RAVO when 'promoting' moves its R forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of approval shouted at a fine performance.

clue.text: Bit of a twist for Tolkien lovers?

indicators.note: a twist here turns the phrase right round so it reads backwards

parts.note: fans of Tolkien's elves could be called elf fans

explanation.surface: A wry aside about a small surprise aimed at fans of The Lord of the Rings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of a twist' reads as a phrase, but 'Bit' is the horse's mouthpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple jointed mouthpiece for a horse is one kind of bridle bit.

clue.text: Tripe and mushrooms, after a time, served up weekly

indicators.note: served up, in a down clue, means the whole string is read bottom to top
after puts the mushrooms behind the a and time

parts.note: tripe, meaning nonsense, is rot
ceps are a kind of mushroom

explanation.surface: A cafe dish of tripe and mushrooms is served once a week after a wait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tripe' wants to be food but means nonsense; ROTATCEPS is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spectator is a long-running British magazine published every week.

clue.text: Wobbly, like a piece of furniture

parts.note: like means as
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Something rickety, like a table with an uneven leg.
explanation.definitionFit: In electronics an astable circuit has no steady state, so it is unstable, oscillating back and forth.

clue.text: Cash regularly received by lightweight English author

indicators.note: received by means the picked letters go inside the weight

parts.note: a gram is a very small unit of weight

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word Cash

explanation.surface: An English writer of slight build is paid cash at intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: Kenneth Grahame wrote The Wind in the Willows.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenneth Grahame was a Scottish-born writer of children's books, so an example of a writer.

clue.text: Fighter in Burma wanting tips for Asian language

indicators.note: wanting tips means losing the first and last letters

parts.note: the Chindits were a British-led special force fighting in Burma in World War Two

explanation.surface: A soldier in Burma lacks the tips of his language.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chindits were a WWII long-range unit in Burma; without its end letters CHINDIT loses C and T.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the most widely spoken tongue of northern India, an example of a language of Asia.

clue.text: To succeed with modern technology, show some sense!

parts.note: a plan that comes off succeeds
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: A sceptic tells a tech enthusiast that gadgets alone won't bring success.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is an idiom telling someone to stop talking nonsense and be reasonable.

clue.text: Male expert in a case involving powerful women

indicators.note: in places the expert inside the court case

parts.note: a case in court is a trial
arch, as in a cunning old hand, stands for an expert

explanation.surface: A male specialist appears in a court case about strong women.
explanation.walkthrough: ARCH sits inside A TRIAL after M; 'in' looks like part of 'expert in a case'.
explanation.definitionFit: A society ruled or headed by women, especially mothers, is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Artillery sent back to Western Front in this?

definitions.text: Artillery sent back to Western Front in this?

indicators.note: the front of the word Western is its first letter
sent back means the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: Gunners shipped back to the Western Front during the First World War.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' attaches AR after W; the Western Front was the main battleground of WWI, so the whole clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Armed conflict between nations is where artillery is sent to the front, so the clue paints the answer itself.

clue.text: Wine lover, terrible glutton

indicators.note: terrible suggests a mess, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wine buff who drinks too much is a dreadful glutton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'glutton' looks like a greedy person but is an animal name.
explanation.definitionFit: Glutton is an old alternative name for the fierce, voracious weasel-like mammal of the north.

clue.text: House seller, say, mostly keen, along with National Trust, to secure that

indicators.note: along with joins the trimmed keenness and the trust abbreviation side by side
to secure means to hold the other piece inside
mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: keen means eager
to say is to state
NT is the National Trust, a British heritage charity

explanation.surface: An eager agent teams up with the National Trust to land a property deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' points back to 'say' as the piece held: EAGE (keen, mostly) and NT surround STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A property agent markets and sells homes, a description of the profession.

clue.text: Bit of money for Indian and European, going short in US city

parts.note: an anna was a small coin of old Indian currency

indicators.note: going short means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a Pole is Polish, a European

explanation.surface: An Indian and a European share a coin while short of cash in America.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Maryland, home of the US Naval Academy, is an example of an American city.

clue.text: Injured medallist's back entering race, being keen

parts.note: an injured leg is lame

indicators.note: entering means the letter goes inside the race

parts.note: a race of people is a nation

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A hurt athlete re-enters the race, eager despite injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keen' wants to mean eager; here it is to wail in grief.
explanation.definitionFit: To keen is to wail for the dead, so the act of keening is mourning aloud, a synonym.

clue.text: Sailor one's left washing up with mum

parts.note: mum is ma, mother

indicators.note: left means the numeral one has gone away
up, in a down clue, means reading bottom to top

parts.note: toilet as in a person's toilet means washing and dressing
one's reads as one has, and one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A sailor is left doing the dishes while Mum watches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'washing up' looks like dishes; 'up' reverses TOILET to TELIOT and losing I leaves TELOT.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a slang word, from French, for a seaman, a synonym.

clue.text: Silky coat not quite all the rage

indicators.note: not quite means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: fury is all-consuming rage

explanation.surface: A silky coat that is nearly the height of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all the rage' wants to mean fashionable; here it is anger.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's soft dense hair is a coat; a pelt of mink or similar is a description.

clue.text: Father nimble, but physically weak

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
nimble means agile

explanation.surface: An agile priest who is nonetheless frail.
explanation.definitionFit: Frail health means delicate or easily harmed, a synonym for bodily weakness.

clue.text: Old farm vehicle fan, sort of

parts.note: ex means former or old
a tractor is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: An enthusiast of vintage farm machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fan' wants to be an enthusiast; it is a ventilator.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen or bathroom ventilator draws out stale air, a kind of electric blower.

clue.text: Bill has little time for paperwork

parts.note: a bill posted up is an ad
min is a minute, a little time

explanation.surface: Bill barely has a moment for the office forms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name; it is an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the informal word for administration, the routine office work.

clue.text: Made phone call after parking accident

indicators.note: after puts the call behind the parking letter

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
rang means telephoned

explanation.surface: Someone telephoned after a mishap in the car park.
explanation.walkthrough: PRANG is British slang for a minor car crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A prang is informal British slang for a minor vehicle crash.

clue.text: Soldier suffered a cut

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
to get an illness is to suffer it, so got means suffered

explanation.surface: A soldier was wounded by a cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a cut' looks like a wound but is meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg of lamb or mutton is a butcher's joint, an example of a meat cut.

clue.text: 3, maybe, is joining car race but failing to finish

indicators.note: failing to finish means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Le Mans is the French twenty-four-hour motor race

explanation.surface: Someone enters a motor race but drops out before the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue at 3 gives HEBRIDEAN, an islander from Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hebridean lives on a Scottish island, so is an example of an island dweller.

clue.text: Fresh set of directions

parts.note: a set of compass directions begins here with north
the further compass points given are east and west

explanation.surface: A new set of instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'directions' looks like instructions but means compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh and recent are synonyms of not previously existing.

clue.text: Putting brakes on endless all night revelling

indicators.note: revelling suggests wild partying, so the letters are jumbled
endless means the word all loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Slowing down after an all-night party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts all to AL; 'revelling' shuffles AL plus NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt something is to stop it, so stopping or slowing is braking.

clue.text: Consumed portion of meat enthusiastically

indicators.note: portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone tucked into a helping of meat with gusto.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been consumed has been swallowed, a synonym.

clue.text: Used properly, time moved on for Spooner

indicators.note: for Spooner means the first sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: a spell is a period of time
went means moved on

explanation.surface: A period of time passes, in Reverend Spooner's tangled speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Spooner swaps the opening sounds of SPELL WENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Money or time put to good purpose is said to be wisely or sensibly expended.
